source_text: Si enim ob unius delictum mors regnavit per unum, multo magis, qui abundantiam gratiae et donum iustitiae accipiunt, in vita regnabunt per unum Iesum Christum [n345] . Consequenter, quod coepit, affirmat; duas enim posuit sententias utrique volens convenire, quod in fine subiunxit. Per unum enim, qui fuit forma peccati et in cuius similitudine praevaricantur sub lege peccantes, pronuntiat regnare mortem, et per unum regnare in vita abundantiam quosque gratiae consecutos, quae gratia virtutem imitantibus prodest. Non remansit ergo de uno quaestio, quia hoc, quod subditum est eos videlicet in vita regnare, qui abundantiam gratiae perceperint, etiam primum illud absolvit, ut nemo videlicet cogatur in mortem, nisi qui exemplum peccantis adamaverit.
pass_a_gloss: For if on account of the offense of one death reigned through one, much more those who receive an abundance of grace and a gift of justice will reign in life through one Jesus Christ. Consequently he affirms what he began; for he placed two sentences, wanting that which he subjoined at the end to fit each. For through one, who was a form of sin and in whose likeness those sinning under the law transgress, he pronounces that death reigns, and through one that those who have obtained an abundance of grace reign in life, which grace profits those imitating virtue. A question therefore has not remained about one, because this which was subjoined, namely that those reign in life who have perceived an abundance of grace, also absolved that first, so that namely no one is compelled into death except he who has loved the example of one sinning.

pass_b_english: ‘For if through one man’s offense death reigned through one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one Jesus Christ’ (Romans 5:17). He consistently confirms what he began. He has set down two statements, intending what he added at the end to apply to both. He declares that death reigns through one who was a model of sin, and in whose likeness those who sin under the law transgress. He also declares that those who have obtained abundant grace reign in life through one—a grace which benefits those who imitate virtue. No question about the ‘one’ therefore remains. The added statement that those who receive abundant grace reign in life also resolves the first statement: no one is driven to death unless he has embraced the sinner’s example.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
